Based on my investigation, I have a clear picture of the issue.

## Analysis

The bug: S3 PUT requests using SigV4 **streaming** uploads (`x-amz-content-sha256: STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD`) send the body in AWS-chunked format (each chunk prefixed with a hex size and `chunk-signature`, as visible in the trace: `93;chunk-signature=...\r\n...\r\n0;chunk-signature=...\r\n\r\n`).

The `Content-MD5` header sent by the SDK is computed over the **decoded payload** (147 bytes), but LocalStack validates it in `check_content_md5(data, headers)` against the **raw chunked body** (320 bytes, including all framing/signatures) — hence the `BadDigest` mismatch.

Key findings:
- `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py:62` defines `STREAMING_HMAC_PAYLOAD = "STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD"` but it is **never used** — the streaming payload is never decoded before MD5 validation.
- `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py:887-901` — `check_content_md5(data, headers)` computes `md5(data)` over the raw request body, which is wrong for aws-chunked/streaming requests.
- `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py:1221-1227` — `forward_request` invokes `check_content_md5(data, headers)` whenever a `Content-MD5` header is present, passing the undecoded body.
- No code anywhere handles `x-amz-decoded-content-length` or decodes the aws-chunked payload (search for `decoded-content-length`, `STREAMING`, `aws_chunked` found only the unused constant).

The fix must live in the S3 proxy listener: decode the aws-chunked streaming body (based on `x-amz-content-sha256 == STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` and `x-amz-decoded-content-length`) before computing the MD5, either inside `check_content_md5` or at the call site in `forward_request`.
